reason: E3 supports that nonequilibrium SRO states form during processing, but none of the cited evidence addresses Mg-containing alloys, SRO-driven intermetallic nucleation, or the link between SRO/intermetallics and corrosion/oxidation resistance. E1 and E2 discuss oxidation and corrosion in Cr-containing HEAs without Mg or SRO, providing no support for the key premises.
premises: Thermal exposure promotes evolution of chemical short-range order (SRO) in HEAs
SRO evolution drives nucleation of intermetallic phases
Mg-containing intermetallics alter surface chemistry and defect structure
Microstructural changes from intermetallics modify corrosion and oxidation resistance
Nonequilibrium SRO states are accessible via processing and differ from equilibrium states
